item.title: World's largest freshwater lake is recovering after decades of decline
item.description: Lake Baikal in Siberia holds around 20% of the world's surface freshwater, making it the most voluminous freshwater lake (Lake Superior on the United States–Canada border is the largest by surface area). This makes the lake one of the most important environments for biodiversity—in fact, it was designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1996 because of this. Yet it has shown considerable decline over the last century, with aridification spreading across East Asia. Fuente: Phys.org.

El problema afectó los sistemas utilizados para coordinar el tráfico aéreo, una herramienta esencial para que los controladores mantengan contacto con las aeronaves y gestionen de forma segura las operaciones en tierra y en vuelo. ¿Qué consecuencias tiene esta falla? Luis Quiñonez, expiloto naval, empresario y experto en seguridad, abordó el tema en France 24. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: US flights resume after nationwide ground stop lifted
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says airplane departures can resume after the agency lifted a nationwide ground stop caused by communications problems. Air travel across the United States had come to a halt earlier on Friday afternoon after the ordered all flights grounded because of a communications breakdown at the regional centres that manage the country’s air traffic. item.description: Next week, US President Donald Trump will engage with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit, despite claims regarding businesswoman Alice Huang and her connection to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang surfacing in the media. item.title: Forcing yourself to smile can actually make you miserable
item.description: Smiling may not always make you happier, and new research suggests that forcing yourself to smile repeatedly could actually make you feel worse. In a University of Florida study involving more than 1,100 participants, researchers discovered that while a single artificial smile can provide a small mood boost, repeatedly faking smiles can erase that benefit or even reverse it. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Same farms, different answers: When nitrogen pollution estimates don't add up
item.description: To reduce nitrogen pollution stemming from synthetic fertilizer and livestock waste, California's Central Valley relies on five data sets to estimate surplus nitrogen. However, most parts of the United States use just one or two data sets—the U.S. Department of Agriculture's agricultural survey and census—to estimate nitrogen surplus. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Common ADHD classroom accommodations may not help students succeed, study finds
item.description: Extra time on assignments. Frequent breaks. A quiet place to work. For students with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), these are some of the most common accommodations schools provide to make learning easier.
